review_definition: Reviewed v1 means all ten investigation lanes were systematically checked. Each lane ends in source-backed findings, a bounded partial finding, or a documented open question with a next action. It does not mean the organisation is fully mapped.

organisations.name: Premium Food Group / Tönnies
organisations.why: Seed case with named farm relationships, slaughter infrastructure, public-money participation and direct lobbying records.
organisations.what_we_know: Named farm relationships, livestock intermediary, group facilities, scale, project participation, lobbying and competition-law history are source-backed. The exact named-farm → slaughterhouse hop remains open.
organisations.next_action: Prove one exact named-farm slaughterhouse destination or preserve the public-access boundary.

organisations.name: Westfleisch SCE mbH
organisations.why: Farmer-owned meat group with a documented cooperative supplier network, five meat centres, legal site operators and group logistics.
organisations.what_we_know: Supplier model, regional supplier population, facilities, live-animal logistics, association links and a higher-husbandry programme are documented. Named farm → named facility remains open.
organisations.next_action: Prove one named farm → named Westfleisch facility relationship and one downstream product/customer edge.

organisations.name: PHW-Gruppe / WIESENHOF
organisations.why: Vertically integrated poultry system spanning parent flocks, hatcheries, feed, contract farms, slaughter, processing and brands.
organisations.what_we_know: Integration, contract-farmer model, brands, broad sales channels, alternative-protein activity and direct Lobbyregister activity are source-backed. Named farm → facility remains open.
organisations.next_action: Resolve one named contract farmer → named slaughter facility and principal German slaughter-site legal operators.

organisations.name: Danish Crown Germany
organisations.why: German site network plus Friland contract-farmer and partner-processing model make it a strong traceability case.
organisations.what_we_know: Current German locations and several site legal entities are documented. Friland documents German contract farmers and partner slaughter/cutting plants, but does not name the exact farm → facility pair in the reviewed source.
organisations.next_action: Name the German Friland contract farmers and partner slaughter plants, then prove one farm → facility path.

organisations.name: Müller Gruppe
organisations.why: Southern German meat group with unusually explicit slaughter-volume and supplier-contract disclosures.
organisations.what_we_know: Group companies, slaughter scale, supplier groups, livestock traders, supply/offtake contracts, Haltungsform-3 incentives and a VDF leadership link are documented.
organisations.next_action: Use the supplier-contract system to prove one named producer → Ulm/Bayreuth/Ingolstadt slaughter-site path.

organisations.name: Plukon Germany
organisations.why: A highly explicit chain across hatcheries, agricultural coordination, growers, slaughter plants, processing and brands.
organisations.what_we_know: Seven German operations, Storkow throughput, Plukon Agri's intermediary role, grower/hatchery relationships, ITW share, FairMast and a historical association-linked lobbying relationship are documented.
organisations.next_action: Name one grower and close the hatchery → Plukon Agri → grower → slaughter-site path.

organisations.name: Rothkötter Unternehmensgruppe
organisations.why: Integrated feed, hatchery, poultry-processing and distribution system with a clear missing farm layer.
organisations.what_we_know: Scale, feed mills, hatchery, Haren/Wietze processing, Landgeflügel distribution and historical association-linked lobbying are documented. Named grower → facility remains open.
organisations.next_action: Resolve the missing agricultural middle: named grower → Rothkötter/Landgeflügel chain → Haren or Wietze.

organisations.name: Sprehe Gruppe
organisations.why: Multi-brand group with contract growers, own controlled slaughter, numerous sites and an explicit holding structure.
organisations.what_we_know: Brand/site footprint, Josef Wernke slaughter/cutting, contract-grower sourcing, Union-Besitz holding structure, organic transition signals and historical association-linked lobbying are documented.
organisations.next_action: Turn the contract-grower statement into one named farm → own slaughter operation → product path.

organisations.name: Arla / former DMK Group
organisations.why: Strong temporal entity-resolution case after the 2026 Arla/DMK combination, with continuing DMK legal entities and direct lobbying records.
organisations.what_we_know: Merger timing, continuing DMK legal status, farmer/milk scale, direct DMK Lobbyregister activity, a narrow public-grants record and historical Bundeskartellamt oversight are documented.
organisations.next_action: Keep temporal identities clean while mapping DMK farmer milk → specific German dairy → brand/product under the new Arla parent structure.

organisations.name: Hochwald Foods
organisations.why: Cooperative dairy system with direct farmer membership, large milk volumes, production sites, quality programmes and brand/acquisition history.
organisations.what_we_know: Group milk/revenue scale, member-farm context, farm-to-Hochwald-plant relationship at group level, programme coverage, Mechernich capacity and Tuffi acquisition history are documented.
organisations.next_action: Prove one member farm → specific Hochwald dairy → named regional brand/product path.
